title: Pre-Analysis — Dual Cargo Smoke Sampling Loop with Cross-Channel Voting
abstract: Closed pre-analysis for the addition of a second cargo smoke sampling loop with cross-channel voting, covering the flow and integrity check, the compartment wiring routes and the false warning troubleshooting procedure.

sections.objective: Establish what a second sampling loop and a voting rule change in the published detection data, find every route and ground provision the second loop has to share with existing installations, and determine whether the voting rule invalidates any procedure that assumes a single detection channel. The order was raised by the fire protection office after a run of false warnings on the forward compartment that the fleet reliability review could not close with the single loop architecture.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and one of them invalidates a published procedure. The flow and integrity check is written for one loop and one detector pair, and its acceptance flow band cannot simply be doubled because the second loop draws from the same compartment volume; the check has to be run per loop with the other isolated. The false warning procedure assumes a single channel throughout and concludes that a warning with no smoke found is a sampling line fault, a conclusion the voting rule makes unsafe. Two wiring findings came from the shared detection FIN and the compartment routes rather than from any text: the second loop shares the forward compartment cable run with the lighting harness, and the aft and bulk ground point layout has no spare stud for the second loop's screen.
sections.next_steps: Release was authorised on condition that the flow check and the false warning procedure are reissued with the modification, and that the aft ground point layout gains two studs before the first production cut in. The wiring office was asked to reroute the second loop clear of the compartment lighting harness rather than sharing the run, on separation grounds. The reliability review was asked to keep the false warning counter open for a year after cut in so that the voting rule can be shown to work.

similarity_seeds: second sampling loop and voting logic in a cargo compartment
smoke warning with no smoke found on inspection

tasks.title: Search detection data on the forward, aft and bulk compartments
Trace the second loop route and ground provisions
Test the false warning logic against the voting rule
Confirm the compartment volume flow budget with the detection supplier

expected_findings.rationale: The procedure assumes a single detection channel from first symptom to conclusion, and it closes a warning with no smoke found as a sampling line fault. Under a voting rule that conclusion is unsafe: two loops that disagree is itself the finding, and the mechanic must be sent to the disagreeing channel rather than to the sampling line.
expected_findings.resolution: Reissue the procedure with the modification, splitting the logic by embodiment condition and adding the channel disagreement branch.

expected_findings.rationale: The flow and integrity check states one acceptance band for one loop drawing on the compartment volume. With two loops the band cannot be doubled, because both draw from the same volume and the second loop changes the pressure the first sees. The check must be run per loop with the other isolated.
expected_findings.resolution: Reissue the task with a per loop procedure, an isolation step and a revised acceptance band agreed with the detection supplier.

expected_findings.rationale: Found through the detection FIN and the compartment route rather than through any text. The second loop as routed shares the forward compartment cable run with the compartment lighting harness for about four metres, which puts both detection channels and a power circuit in one bundle.
expected_findings.resolution: Reroute the second loop clear of the lighting harness on separation grounds, and show the new route on the sheet before the production cut in.

expected_findings.rationale: The aft and bulk compartment ground point layout has no spare stud at the position the second loop's screen has to terminate. Adding a stud is a small change but it has to be embodied in the same slot, since a loop installed without its screen terminated cannot be released to service.
expected_findings.resolution: Add two studs to the aft ground point layout and declare the change concurrent with the modification.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the forward and aft compartment zones and is retrieved by both passes because it is the access task most often run before any work in those compartments. Removing a lining panel is unchanged by the second loop; the panel is removed the same way whether one or two sampling lines run above it.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2018-03-27. One invalidated procedure, one task reissue and two wiring actions. Cleared to proceed with the ground point change embodied concurrently.
